question.problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨-t,\,1,\,{t}^{2}⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s}.$
question.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,2t⟩, \\ v(1) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,2⟩, \\ a(1) & =⟨0,\,0,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(1)\cdot a(1)$ and $||v(1)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1)\cdot a(1) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,2⟩ \\  & =4, \\ ||v(1)|| & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(0)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=1,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(1)\cdot a(1)}{||v(1)||} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{5}\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$
